title: Reductivity, maximal tori, and scheme-theoretic centralizer points
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $T,G$ group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme]. Use closed and normal subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and connectedness [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Use the affine finite-type predicate and smooth faithful-matrix unipotence of [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure], and scalar extension, the algebraic closure, and tori of [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. An inclusion $i:T\to G$ is a maximal torus if it is a closed subgroup inclusion, $T$ is a torus, and for every closed torus inclusion $j:S\to G$, every homomorphism $f:T\to S$ satisfying $j\circ f=i$ is an isomorphism. The group $G$ is reductive if it is affine of finite type and smooth over $k$, its extension to $\bar k$ is connected, and every smooth connected normal closed unipotent subgroup of $G_{\bar k}$ is isomorphic to the trivial group scheme. For a group-scheme homomorphism $i:T\to G$ and a commutative $k$-algebra $A$, define $C_i(A)$ to be the subset of $G(A)$ consisting of $g$ such that for every commutative $k$-algebra $B$ and every $k$-algebra map $f:A\to B$, the image of $g$ in $G(B)$ commutes with $i(t)$ for every $t\in T(B)$. There is no reducedness assumption on $A$ or $B$.
